title: Video Repurposer Content Plan
description: Editorial output of the content-analysis + clip-selection skills for one source recording. Independent of any editing tool. The `keep_segments` of each clip (start/end, seconds into the SOURCE video) are exactly the spans render_clips.py cuts from the source.

video_id.description: Stable slug for the source recording, e.g. zoom-2026-09-01-ai-strategy

source_video.description: Path to the source file, relative to project root, e.g. input/zoom-2026-09-01.mp4

transcript_source.description: Path to the transcript JSON this plan was derived from

presenter_label.description: Speaker label used for the primary presenter in the transcript, e.g. PRESENTER

name_timestamps.description: Put the source range in every clip name - "16 How to discover topics (0.58.49-1.04.40)". true for the whole recording, or a clip number to start there so clips already in the tracker and in Drive keep their names.

rejected_sections.description: Editorial record of source sections that were considered and NOT turned into a clip, with why. Not required to cover the whole recording.

video_name.description: Short label for the recording (e.g. 'ICP'). Becomes the tracker's Video column so rows filter by source.

why_standalone.description: Why this section is worth turning into a standalone video

source_start.description: Exact source start timestamp, seconds. Equals the first keep_segment's start.

source_end.description: Exact source end timestamp, seconds. Equals the last keep_segment's end.

duration_sec.description: Runtime of the FINISHED clip = sum of keep_segments durations. NOT source_end - source_start, which is only the source window and is wider whenever anything is cut out of the middle. The 300s (5 min) cap applies to this runtime.

keep_segments.description: Presenter-only sections to KEEP, in source-clip seconds. render_clips.py cuts exactly these, in order.

remove_segments.description: Sections inside [source_start, source_end] to cut out (rambling, repetition, weak explanation, etc.)

other_speaker_segments.description: Sections where a speaker other than the presenter is talking

filler_segments.description: Filler / low-value sections (false starts, rambling asides, throat-clearing)

recommended_hook.description: Suggested opening framing/line for the clip

recommended_ending.description: Suggested closing framing/line for the clip

transcript.description: Complete verbatim transcript of the proposed clip (concatenated keep_segments only). The presenter's words are never rewritten.

short_name.description: 3-6 word label. Numbered by source order it becomes the clip name: '01 What is an ICP' - the rendered filename, the SRT name and the sheet's Clip name.

topic.description: The subject area, a few words. Tracker column.

summary.description: The points actually discussed in this clip. Tracker column.

score.description: Publish-worthiness out of 10, shown in the review table. Should agree directionally with confidence_score (a 9/10 clip is not 0.4 confidence) without being a mechanical confidence x 10.

score_reasoning.description: Why that score - what is strong, what it was marked down for. This is what the user reads when deciding to veto.

hook_line.description: The clip's opening line as the viewer hears it. Distinct from recommended_hook, which is editorial advice about how to open.

callouts.description: Optional pop-up boxes that slide in from the right, hold, and slide out. Used to explain a name the viewer won't know (e.g. the presenter's company).

at.description: Source seconds - usually when the presenter says the name.

label.description: Small heading above the text, e.g. the company name.

pinned.description: Placed by hand (x/y/side); place_callouts leaves it alone.

long_approved.description: The user approved this clip over the duration cap so a topic isn't cut short; the validator warns instead of failing.

append_after_existing.description: Added after the set was published: numbered after every other clip so existing numbers don't shift. Use 1, 2, 3... for successive late batches so earlier additions keep their numbers.

slide_cover.description: Optional: paint over part of the slide for the whole clip and optionally add new text there - e.g. replace a slide title that doesn't match what the clip is about. Drawn under captions and pop-ups.

box.description: [x0, y0, x1, y1] to cover, as fractions of the frame. With "image", the region of the still to show, at the same place.

image.description: Path to a full-resolution still (e.g. work/stills/<stem>_<slide>.png) held over the clip for this from/to, so a slide stays on screen while the recording wanders off it. Give one entry per region so the live camera tile keeps moving.

fill.description: Cover colour, e.g. #FFFFFF. Match it to the rendered slide background.

text.description: Text drawn on the cover, e.g. a replacement slide title.

text_at.description: [x, y] top-left of the text, as fractions of the frame.

color.description: Text colour - match the slide's title colour.

size.description: Font size as a fraction of the frame height.

font.description: Font name from assets/fonts. Default Inter.

align.description: ASS numpad anchor for text_at: 7 top-left (default), 5 centre - a title card on an empty slide.

from.description: Source seconds the cover starts. Default: clip start.

to.description: Source seconds the cover ends - e.g. only an opening line borrowed from another slide. Default: clip end.
